claim.claim-text: a nerve stimulation device (110) configured to deliver a series of low current electrical impulses to a nerve to produce only sub-visible muscle responses; and a recording device (120) configured to record electrical activity associated with an evoked muscle response caused by the series of low current electrical impulses; characterized in that: the low current electrical impulses that the nerve stimulation device (110) is configured to deliver are between 0.2 mA - 4 mA.
2. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1,

wherein the paralysis monitoring system (100) is configured to administer a calibration signal with the nerve stimulation device (110) and record a baseline muscle response with the recording device (120); and wherein the paralysis monitoring system (100) is configured to compare subsequent recorded muscle responses to the baseline muscle response.

3. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1, wherein the nerve stimulation device is configured to transmit electrical impulses to a patient (500) based on a body mass index of the patient (500).

4. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 3, wherein the nerve stimulation device is configured to transmit electrical impulses in the range of about 0.5 millivolts to 1.5 millivolts to patients having a body mass index in a first range; and wherein the nerve stimulation device is configured to transmit electrical impulses in the range of about 1.5 millivolts to 4 millivolts to patients having a body mass index in a second range that is higher than the first range.
5. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1, wherein the nerve stimulation device and the recording device (120) are disposed on a strip (130).
6. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1, wherein the recording device (120) comprises an electrode or a needle.
7. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1, wherein the nerve stimulation device comprises a transcutaneous electrode probe configured to transmit milliamp current.
8. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1, wherein the nerve stimulation device is configured to provide the low current electrical impulses on an automatic cycling schedule.

9. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1, said recording device (120) being a first recording device, and said paralysis monitoring system (100) further comprising a second recording device configured to record electrical activity associated with the series of low current electrical impulses to the nerve;

wherein the first recording device (120) is configured to be placed over a target muscle group associated with the nerve; and wherein the second recording device is configured to be disposed away from the target muscle group.

10. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 9, wherein the nerve stimulation device and the first recording device are disposed along a first axis, wherein the nerve stimulation device and the second recording device (120) are disposed along a second axis, and wherein the first axis and the second axis intersect at a nonzero angle.

11. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 9, wherein the first recording device is disposed substantially further from the nerve stimulation device than the second recording device.

12. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 9, wherein the nerve stimulation device and the first recording device are disposed on a strip of material; and wherein, preferably, the second recording device is disposed on a second strip that connects to the first strip.
13. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1,

wherein the paralysis monitoring system (100) is configured to apply an intermittent pulse that is repeated periodically; and wherein the paralysis monitoring system (100) is further configured to measure and record a response to the intermittent pulse to determine an effect of a paralytic agent.

14. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1, wherein the recording device (120) is configured to record a spike focus of the evoked muscle response, i.e. spike discharges produced by the stimulated muscle.

15. The paralysis monitoring system (100) according to claim 1, further comprising an alarm configured to provide an alert upon detecting a return of response signals or muscle activity of a patient (500).
